question: Do independently trained text, image, environmental-audio and silent-video encoders preserve similar relationships between the same concepts, at different semantic granularities and information constraints?

conditions.paired: average of A-A and B-B; same complete recordings in the two representations
conditions.cross_source: average of A-B and B-A; no source, normalized author or uploader shared across folds

primary_pilot_statistic: cross-source concept-centroid Spearman RSA with global and taxonomy-preserving label nulls
multiple_testing: One Holm family over every registered pair and estimable condition/null combination for ordinal RSA; missing estimands retain their slots as p=1.
test_direction: upper tail; finite Monte Carlo correction (1 + count) / (1 + permutations)
uncertainty: percentile interval from common exponential creator-component weights within the fixed roster; leave-one-group-out range separately; conditional sensitivity, no population coverage guarantee
metric: fit nonnegative zero-intercept scale on disjoint development concepts, assess relative RMSE and constant comparator on held-out concepts, and repeat fitting in every permuted draw
subset_rules: pairwise finite/nonzero complete sources; retain concepts with >=2 per fold; balance fold sizes by source ID; use same units in paired and cross-source conditions

native_gate.classification: verified native encoder without explicit cross-modal alignment training
native_gate.applied_policy: do not run empirical alignment utility before reproducible native geometry; the present sample is for contextual geometry
